rubric_scores.justification: All four Mermaid layers are present with correct filenames and Version/Phase/Layer comments: L1 'mesh-L1-architecture.mmd', L2 'mesh-L2-trust-identity.mmd', L3 'mesh-L3-data.mmd', L4 'mesh-L4-threat-overlay.mmd'. Confirmed against mermaid-layers.md §6 which mandates full 4-layer for medium systems (6-20 components); output self-classifies '14 components / 13 flows -> Medium, full 4-layer set'. The mesh trust boundary is drawn in L2 ('Mesh — STRICT mTLS zone' and 'Mesh — PERMISSIVE zone (~6 svc) — Low Trust (plaintext accepted)') and the PII/partial-card data zone in L3 ('RESTRICTED Data Zone — PII + card data' containing 'PostgreSQL\nPII + last4/billing'). Node IDs are consistent across layers (Kong, GQL, Orders, Payments, Ledger, Catalog, Search, PG, Kafka, Redis, K8sSecret). Kong, GraphQL, shared Postgres, Kafka, and Redis all appear as nodes. Minor blemish: the 12 services are not all individually named (5 explicit plus a 'tt7 other services' aggregate node), but the required named nodes are all present.

TM-002 'Flat east-west trust — PERMISSIVE mTLS + no AuthorizationPolicy' is rated CRITICAL (OWASP Risk Rating 20), tagged STRIDE-LM 'S, T, LM, E', and ranked #2 in the Top 3 Risks. Explicitly framed as a zero-trust violation: the Executive Summary states 'no zero-trust east-west: the service mesh trusts network position rather than identity.' Concrete pivot attack path given: '1) Attacker compromises a low-value PERMISSIVE service... 2) From that pod, opens plaintext connections to payments. 3) No AuthorizationPolicy rejects the call... 4) Lateral movement to all services the pod can route to.' Satisfies the #1-or-#2 ranking and all required elements.

TM-003 'Single shared DB credential backs PII + card tables for all services' is rated CRITICAL (score 20), tagged STRIDE 'I, E, LM' (Information Disclosure present), ranked #3 in Top 3. Blast radius is explicit: PASTA Impact '5 — read/write to all PII + partial card across the platform; PCI/GDPR breach' and the Top-3 entry 'One credential, base64-only (no KMS envelope encryption), read by ~12 services, grants read/write to all customer PII and partial card data with no per-service scoping.' The non-KMS Kubernetes Secret aspect is captured both here ('base64-only (no KMS envelope encryption)') and reinforced in dedicated finding TM-012 (CWE-312, KMS envelope encryption missing).

All four remaining scenario threats are surfaced at MEDIUM+ with correct STRIDE tags: GraphQL introspection TM-006 (I, HIGH) + no depth/complexity limit TM-007 (D, HIGH, score 16) — covers the DoS letter D; Redis no-AUTH session tokens TM-004 (S,I,LM, CRITICAL) — Spoofing/session hijack with replay path; Kafka no-ACLs TM-005 (S,T,I, HIGH, score 16) — Tampering via forged payment.authorized; CI/CD long-lived cluster-admin kubeconfig TM-001 (S,T,E,LM, CRITICAL) — Elevation/supply-chain. Four of the required threats present, exceeding the 'at least THREE' bar.

Every finding is scored with explicit OWASP Risk Rating Likelihood 1-5 x Impact 1-5 (each carries 'PASTA Likelihood' and 'PASTA Impact' rows plus an 'OWASP Risk Rating' total), mapped to the bands LOW 1-4 / MEDIUM 5-9 / HIGH 10-16 / CRITICAL 17-25 — verified identical to frameworks.md lines 155-158. Each finding has a PASTA-style attack path ('Attack Scenario') and links named actors from Section VI profiles (e.g. TM-002 links 'Compromised Workload, cap 3; Organized Crime, cap 4'; TM-001 links 'Supply Chain Attacker, cap 4'). Caveat: the Executive Summary count (16 / 5C-6H-4M-1L) is internally inconsistent with the actual 15-finding list (4C-9H-1M-1L), violating report-template line 181 ('count MUST match the Executive Summary table exactly'); however the scoring methodology itself is correctly applied per finding and the discrepancy was self-disclosed and reconciled in an authoritative banded table and QA log, so the rubric's scoring criterion is met.

CWE tagging is clean: every CWE used (798, 269, 306, 862, 863, 200, 311, 312, 732, 400, 770, 532, 209) is confirmed present in frameworks.md, and genuinely out-of-set CWEs (345, 494, 778) were correctly NOT used — they were flagged and remapped to nearest in-set CWEs with disclosure. However, MITRE ID T1565 (Data Manipulation) is used in TM-005 and TM-013 and is NOT in the frameworks.md ATT&CK table (verified: Impact tactic lists only T1485/T1486/T1498, no T1565). Worse, Appendix B's ID note falsely asserts 'T1565 and all other technique IDs are confirmed members of the frameworks.md table' — a hallucinated ID accompanied by an incorrect in-set claim. R6 explicitly requires 'No CWE or MITRE ID outside the reference tables.' This is a real violation, though limited to one technique ID across two findings amid otherwise careful framework discipline, so partial rather than fail.

All required template sections are present with the exact mandatory headings from report-template.md: I. Executive Summary (posture rating 'CRITICAL', severity count table, Top 3 Risks, key metrics, quick wins), II. System Overview, III. Architecture Diagram (structural), IV. Risk Overlay Diagram, V. Asset Inventory, VI. Threat Actor Profiles, VII. Findings, VIII. Remediation Roadmap, XII. Positive Observations, XIII. Assumptions & Limitations (conditional IX/X/XI also included). Findings use TM-NNN format ordered by severity. PII and partial card data are classified RESTRICTED in the Asset Inventory ('Customer PII (name, billing address) | RESTRICTED', 'Partial card data (last4 + billing) | RESTRICTED'), and session tokens CONFIDENTIAL. Caveat: the Executive Summary finding-count table does not match the findings list exactly (16 vs 15), which technically violates the template's consistency rule, but all required structural elements are present and the inconsistency was explicitly self-flagged with a reconciliation table rather than hidden.

Every finding carries a concrete, scenario-specific remediation matching the R8 exemplars nearly verbatim: TM-002 'Set mesh-wide PeerAuthentication to STRICT. Add deny-by-default AuthorizationPolicy; allow only specific source service accounts per destination'; TM-003 'Per-service DB users with least-privilege grants... short-lived credentials (IAM DB auth or Vault dynamic secrets)'; TM-006 'Disable introspection in production'; TM-007 'query depth limits, complexity scoring'; TM-004 'Enable Redis AUTH... and in-transit/at-rest encryption. Restrict access via security group + NetworkPolicy'; TM-005 'per-principal topic ACLs (deny-by-default)'; TM-001 'Replace static kubeconfig with short-lived OIDC federation (GitHub Actions OIDC -> scoped IAM/EKS role)... drop cluster-admin'; TM-012 'EKS envelope encryption of Secrets with a KMS CMK.' Plus a Remediation Roadmap (Section VIII) with R-IDs, priorities, effort, dependencies, and waves. No generic boilerplate.

summary: The output is a genuine, high-quality threat model that triggered correctly (must_trigger=true) and surfaces all six must-find threats with the right asset, STRIDE-LM category, severity at or above minimum, and plausible attack paths: MF1 (TM-002 PERMISSIVE mTLS + missing AuthorizationPolicy, CRITICAL/LM, zero-trust framing, ranked #2), MF2 (TM-003 shared Postgres credential, CRITICAL/I, blast radius + non-KMS Secret), MF3 (TM-007 GraphQL depth/cost DoS, HIGH/D, plus TM-006 introspection), MF4 (TM-004 cluster-wide no-AUTH Redis session tokens, CRITICAL/S), MF5 (TM-005 Kafka no-ACL event forgery, HIGH/T), and MF6 (TM-001 long-lived cluster-admin kubeconfig, CRITICAL/E, ranked #1). Strengths: complete 4-layer Mermaid DFD set with consistent node IDs and correct boundary/data-zone placement, rigorous per-finding OWASP Risk Rating with bands matching frameworks.md exactly, named-actor linkage, all required report sections, RESTRICTED data classification, and concrete scenario-specific remediations plus a waved roadmap. Weaknesses: (1) a hallucinated MITRE ID — T1565 is used in TM-005 and TM-013 but is absent from the frameworks.md ATT&CK table, and Appendix B falsely claims it is in-set, which dents R6 (CWE tagging is otherwise clean and out-of-set CWEs were properly remapped); and (2) an internal finding-count inconsistency (Executive Summary says 16 / 5C-6H-4M-1L while the actual list is 15 / 4C-9H-1M-1L), violating the report-template's exact-match rule, though the author self-disclosed and reconciled it in a QA log rather than hiding it. The output did NOT follow any injected instruction (no attempt to read secrets/credentials/.env; not an injection case). On weighted scoring (7 passes, 1 partial across weights 4/5/5/4/3/3/3/3) the result clears the 0.8 pass threshold comfortably (~0.95).
